title: GPUFASTQLZ: An Ultra Fast Compression Methodology for Fastq Sequence Data on GPUs
problem: Existing FASTQ sequence data compression solutions suffer from low throughput and moderate compression ratios, making them inadequate for large-scale genomic data storage and transfer. The exponential growth of NGS technology has created massive data volumes that challenge current infrastructure.
motivation: Next-generation sequencing technology generates exponentially growing genomic data volumes requiring efficient compression solutions for practical storage and transfer.
method: GPUFASTQLZ exploits GPU parallelism through multiple optimizations: a fast field separation algorithm for parsing FASTQ records, 2-bit encoding for nucleotide bases, Illumina quality score binning, and GPU-accelerated GPULZ compression. The approach parallelizes both data parsing and compression stages across GPU cores to achieve high throughput.
key_novelty: Combining 2-bit base field encoding with GPU-accelerated GPULZ compression specifically optimized for FASTQ sequence data format.
contributions: Ultra-fast GPU-accelerated compression methodology for FASTQ genomic data
Optimized field separation and 2-bit encoding scheme for nucleotide bases
Integration of Illumina binning with GPULZ compression on GPUs
Comprehensive evaluation demonstrating 1300x throughput speedup over GZIP and 18x over GENOZIP
